text: The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was born in 1988.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, lives in Khimki in the Moscow Region.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, was born in 1985.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, lives in Zhukovskiy in the Moscow Region.
The applicants were represented by Mr Rachkovskiy, a lawyer practising in Moscow.
The applicants were represented by Ms N. Dobreva, a lawyer practising in Sofia.
The Government were represented initially by Mr G. Matyushkin, Representative of the Russian Federation to the European Court of Human Rights.
The Government were subsequently represented by Mr M. Galperin, successor to Mr G. Matyushkin as Representative of the Russian Federation to the European Court of Human Rights.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.
The background facts relating to the planning, conduct and dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square are set out in more detail in Frumkin v. Russia (no. 74568/12, §§ 7-65, 5 January 2016).

The background facts relating to the planning, conduct and dispersal of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square are set out in more detail in Yaroslav Belousov v. Russia (nos. 2653/13 and 60980/14, §§ 7-33, 4 October 2016).
On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration of 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration of 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The approved meeting at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 was supposed to end at 7.30 p.m.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.

When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it transpired that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue, allegedly restricting the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, a police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered the organisers of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square to finish the meeting early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
It took the police about two hours to clear the protestors from Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened a criminal investigation into suspected acts of mass disorder, an offence under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened a criminal investigation into suspected violence against the police, an offence under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 18 May 2012 the criminal investigation file opened on 6 May 2012 was transferred to the headquarters of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation for further investigation.
On 28 May 2012 another criminal investigation was launched into the offence of organising acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 28 May 2012 the two criminal cases concerning the events at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 were joined.

On 16 December 2013 the Investigative Committee disjoined the case against the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, and the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, and their two co-defendants from the main criminal case file concerning the mass disorder at Bolotnaya Square.
At the time of the events of 6 May 2012, the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was a student working part-time.

section_path: 1. The first applicant's arrest and administrative conviction

text: On 14 April 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow began the trial in a criminal case against four participants in the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square, including both the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, and the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov.

The four defendants at the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow trial beginning 14 April 2014 were charged with participation in acts of mass disorder and committing acts of violence against police officers.

On 25 July 2014, during a court hearing, the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, requested that the court grant a stay of proceedings in respect of the charges under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation on the grounds that the acts with which he was charged were covered by the administrative offence of which he had been convicted on 8 May 2012.
On 25 July 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found no grounds to grant the first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, request for a stay of proceedings.
On an unspecified date police officer A., the alleged victim of the first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, assault, was questioned as a witness during the trial.
Police officer A. testified that when he had been arresting one of the active participants of the demonstration, someone had pulled his helmet and bullet-proof vest, blocking his access to air.
Police officer A. testified that he had fallen to the ground and when he had tried to get up, someone had pushed him again, causing him to fall.
Police officer A. testified that when he had managed to stand up, he had seen a young man whom he had later identified as the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, who had then disappeared in the crowd.
Police officer A. testified that he had felt pain as a result of the first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, actions but had not asked for medical assistance.

Police officer D., questioned as a witness during the trial, testified that he had seen the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, holding on to police officer A.'s bullet-proof vest and trying to push him to the ground.
On 18 August 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, guilty as charged.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that on 6 May 2012, at 5 p.m. at the latest, the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, arrived at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow to take part in the demonstration.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that between 5 p.m. and 10 p.m. on 6 May 2012, the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, took part in acts of mass disorder.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, acting with intent, used violence against police officer A. which did not pose a threat to the life or health of that officer.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, acting with intent with the aim of using violence, tried to prevent police officers from arresting aggressive participants of the demonstration.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, standing behind police officer A., grabbed the latter's bullet-proof vest with his right hand and his anti-riot helmet with his left hand and, acting together with an unidentified person, dragged police officer A. away and then pushed him to the ground.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, actions caused police officer A. pain.

The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, pleaded not guilty to the crime under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation but partially confessed to the use of violence against a public official under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, testified at trial that when police officers had started using force, special means and truncheons against participants in the demonstration, he had heard a cry for help and had seen a man lying on the ground.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, testified at trial that a police officer, who had later turned out to be police officer A., had been bent over the man on the ground, beating him with a truncheon.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, testified at trial that he had grabbed police officer A.'s uniform and pulled it up, and had not hit or pushed anyone.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, testified at trial that police officer A. had not fallen to the ground as a result of the first applicant's actions.

The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, testified at trial that he was aware that by grabbing police officer A.'s uniform, he had committed a crime under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, testified at trial that he did not deny that afterwards he had been standing in a line with others impeding the police from arresting the demonstrators.

The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, testified at trial that on 6 May 2012 he had been arrested, taken to the police station and convicted by a justice of the peace under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that it had not established any facts showing unlawful behaviour on the part of the police during the demonstration on 6 May 2012.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the police officers acted lawfully during the demonstration on 6 May 2012.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow rejected the first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, argument that the criminal proceedings and his prosecution should be terminated on the grounds that he had already been subjected to administrative liability for the same act.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that on 8 May 2012 the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was convicted of failure to obey a lawful order of the police under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, participation in mass disorder and his use of violence against a public official were not covered by the scope of the offence provided for in Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation, as the administrative offence and the crimes had different objects and were committed at different times, albeit consecutively.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow relied on a video recording showing how the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, had grabbed police officer A.'s bullet-proof vest and helmet and had pushed him.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow relied on records of identification parades, according to which police officer A. had identified the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, as the man who had used violence against police officer A.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow relied on records of identification parades, according to which police officer D. had identified the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, as the man who had used violence against police officer A.

The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment, calculated on the basis of a two-year prison term under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation running partly concurrently with a term of one year under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, pre-trial detention counted towards his prison sentence.
On 27 November 2014 the Moscow City Court upheld the first-instance judgment convicting the first applicant, Mr Gushchin.
The Moscow City Court dismissed the first applicant's, Mr Gushchin's, allegation that he had been tried and convicted twice for the same offence.
The first applicant, Mr Gushchin, was released on 8 August 2015 having served his prison term.
At the time of his arrest, the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, was working as a financial consultant.

section_path: 1. The second applicant's arrest and pre-trial detention

text: On 14 April 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow began the hearing of the criminal case against the first applicant, Mr Gushchin, the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, and two co-defendants.

The hearings of the criminal case at the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow took place in hearing room no. 403 of the courthouse, which was equipped with metal cages in which the defendants were held during the hearings.

The hearings of the criminal case at the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow took place in hearing room no. 410 of the courthouse, which was equipped with metal cages in which the defendants were held during the hearings.

One hearing during the first-instance trial took place at the Moscow City Court in hearing room no. 338, which was equipped with a glass cabin (for the description of conditions of detention in that room, see Yaroslav Belousov v. Russia, nos. 2653/13 and 60980/14, §§ 74-75, 4 October 2016).
In its judgment of 18 August 2014, the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, guilty as charged.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that on 6 May 2012 at 5 p.m. at the latest, the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, arrived at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow to take part in the demonstration.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that between 5 p.m. and 8 p.m. on 6 May 2012, the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, took part in acts of mass disorder.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, acting with intent, used violence against police officer I. which did not pose a threat to the life or health of that officer.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, tried to prevent police officers, including police officer I., from arresting another protestor.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, grabbed police officer I. by the leg and, using violence together with unidentified persons, dragged police officer I. away from the protestor and pulled him to the ground.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that unidentified persons hit police officer I. in the head at least twice following the second applicant's, Mr Gaskarov's, actions.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that as a result of the second applicant's, Mr Gaskarov's, and other persons' actions, the protestor was able to escape from the police.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, acting with intent, also used violence against police officer B. by pulling the latter by the left arm and abruptly pulling police officer B. out of the chain of police officers, thereby breaking the chain and making a passage in it for those participating in the mass disorder.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the second applicant's, Mr Gaskarov's, actions caused police officer B. physical pain.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, pleaded not guilty at trial.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, testified at trial that he had been in front of the cordon when the clashes had begun and had pulled police officer B. by the arm but had not hit him.

The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, testified at trial that he had seen a group of police officers trying to arrest a young man, pushing him to the ground, grabbing him by his legs and, as the second applicant had thought, beating the man with truncheons.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, testified at trial that he had approached police officer I. and dragged him away to a metre's distance, without using violence.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, testified at trial that the young man had then stood up and run in the direction of the crowd, and police officer I. had followed him.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, testified at trial that he had seen a few protestors approach police officer I. and hit him at least twice.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, testified at trial that during the demonstration on 6 May 2012 he had been beaten up by the police without any reason.

The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, testified at trial that he had lodged a criminal complaint of ill-treatment with the law-enforcement authorities but they had refused to open a criminal investigation into his allegations.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that it had not established any facts showing unlawful behaviour on the part of the police during the demonstration on 6 May 2012.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held that the police officers acted lawfully during the demonstration on 6 May 2012.

The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, was sentenced to three years and six months' imprisonment, calculated on the basis of a three-year prison term under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, to run partly concurrently with a term of one year and six months under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The second applicant's, Mr Gaskarov's, pre-trial detention counted towards his prison sentence.
On 27 November 2014 the Moscow City Court upheld the first-instance judgment convicting the second applicant, Mr Gaskarov.
The second applicant, Mr Gaskarov, was released on 27 October 2016 having served his prison term.

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder, accompanied by violence, riots, arson, destruction of property, the use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 3 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the instigation of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1, or the instigation of participation in such acts, or the instigation of violence against citizens, shall be punishable by a restriction of liberty for up to two years, or community service for up to two years, or deprivation of liberty for the same term.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation of 30 December 2001, in force at the material time, provided that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of the officer's official duties relating to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the officer's performance of his or her official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between RUB 500 and RUB 1,000 or by administrative detention for up to fifteen days.
